[[File:Vintage Casio Scientific Graphing Pocket Calculator, Model fx-7000GA, Made in Japan, 1990 (8721201872).jpg|thumb|upright|The successor FX-7000 GA was released in 1990.<ref>[https://www.calculator.org/calculators/Casio_fx-7000GA.html calculator.org]</ref>]]
The '''Casio FX-7000G''' is a [[calculator]] which is widely known as being the world's first [[graphing calculator]] available to the public. It was introduced to the public and later manufactured between 1985 and {{circa|1989}}.<ref name=VinTech /> Notable features are its ability to graph functions,<ref name=ChapterFour /> and that it is [[Programmable calculator|programmable]]. The calculator offers 82 scientific functions and is capable of manual computation for basic [[arithmetic]] problems.<ref name=ChapterOne />

==Features==

===Mathematical===
The calculator can compute basic arithmetic functions with a precision up to 13 digits.<ref name=VinTech /> Many functions integrated into the calculator include arithmetic and algebraic computations such as:

*[[square roots]]
*[[multiplicative inverse|reciprocals]]
*[[exponential functions]]
*[[factorials]]
*[[logarithms]]
*[[trig functions]]<ref name=ChapterOne />

Other specialized functions also implemented into the calculator include [[Hyperbolic function|hyperbolic]] and [[statistical]] functions, [[Binary number|binary]]/[[octal]]/[[hexadecimal]]/[[sexagesimal]] conversions and graph plotting.<ref name=ChapterTwo>{{cite web |title=Manual: Chapter 2 |url=http://www.silrun.de/casio/fx7000/manual/Chapter2.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051216091146/http://silrun.de/casio/fx7000/manual/Chapter2.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=2005-12-16 }}</ref>

===Programming===
Like many [[Casio]] calculators, the FX-7000G includes a [[Mathematical programming|programming]] mode,<ref name=ChapterFour>{{cite web |title=Manual: Chapter 4 |url=http://www.silrun.de/casio/fx7000/manual/Chapter4.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031216054750/http://www.silrun.de/casio/fx7000/manual/Chapter4.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=2003-12-16 }}</ref> in addition to its display and graphing mode. It holds 422 bytes of programming memory,<ref name=Specifications>{{cite book|title=fx-7000G Owner's Manual: Specifications}}</ref> less than half a kilobyte.
The calculator uses a [[Lexical analysis#Tokenization|tokenized]] programming language (similar to the earlier FX-602P) which is well suited to writing more complex programs, as memory efficiency is a priority. Tokenization is performed by using characters and symbols in place of long lines of code to minimize the amount of memory being used. The User Manual programming catalog is written in these symbols,<ref name=ChapterFive /> allowing for lengthier programs to be written with less effort and less memory. One example is a program which estimates a [[definite integral]] through the use of [[Simpson's Rule]]; this can be found within the user manual for reference.<ref name=ChapterFive>{{cite web |title=Manual: Chapter 5 |url=http://www.silrun.de/casio/fx7000/manual/Chapter5.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031217095639/http://www.silrun.de/casio/fx7000/manual/Chapter5.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=2003-12-17 }}</ref>

The calculator has 26 numeric memories as standard. Additional memories can be created by reducing the number of bytes available for programs. Using this facility allows a total of 78 memories maximum.

===Graphing===
The calculator has a built in graphing feature which is unique to its model. The calculator can display either built-in graphs that are already programmed or display a user defined graph.<ref name=ChapterThree>{{cite web |title=Manual: Chapter 3 |url=http://www.silrun.de/casio/fx7000/manual/Chapter3.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031216013349/http://www.silrun.de/casio/fx7000/manual/Chapter3.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=2003-12-16 }}</ref> The user also has the option to rewrite any of the previously programmed graphs.<ref name=ChapterThree />
<br>
Statistical graphs can also be generated: bar graphs, line graphs, normal distribution curves, regression lines.<ref name="Specifications"/>

==Display and exterior==

===Display===
The FX-7000G incorporates an [[LCD]] [[Dot Matrix]] design via the display window. When set into character mode the calculator can display up to sixteen characters on each of its eight display lines.<ref name=ChapterOne /> This sixteen character by eight line display is screened on the 96&nbsp;×&nbsp;64 dot matrix.<ref name=ChapterOne>{{cite web |title=Manual: Chapter 1 |url=http://www.silrun.de/casio/fx7000/manual/Chapter1.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040615165644/http://www.silrun.de/casio/fx7000/manual/Chapter1.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=2004-06-15 }}</ref> The LCD is not capable of colour or grey scale display.

===Exterior===
A black casing surrounds the calculator along with a metal panel implemented on the rear; a large plastic screen protects the LCD window as well. Keys are labeled and printed on orange, green, blue, red, and black malleable buttons.<ref name=VinTech />

===Measurements===
The calculator's dimensions (width, height, depth) are {{convert|83.5|x|167|x|14|mm|abbr=on}}. It has an approximate mass of {{convert|155.5|g|abbr=on}} including batteries.
<ref name=VinTech>{{cite web |title=Vintage Technology |url=http://www.vintage-technology.info/pages/calculators/lcd/casiofx7k.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120913082240/http://vintage-technology.info/pages/calculators/lcd/casiofx7k.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=2012-09-13 |access-date=2012-02-14 }}</ref>

===Power===
The Casio Fx-7000G needs a 9.0 volt [[Direct current|DC current]] [[lithium battery]] supply provided by 3 [[CR2032 battery|CR2032]] type cells. The calculator does not accept an [[AC adapter]] and only uses batteries. The average battery life is around 120 hours which is shorter in length compared to similar models.<ref name=VinTech />
